column2: Not Required - If the agent is never connected to a live representative, then a disclosure is not required, or on a multiple account call, the opening and disclosure is only required on the first account.
column3: Incomplete - The Agent fails to introduce themselves or their company, and fails to provide the required call recording disclosure.
column4: Poor - The Agent provides a partial introduction (e.g., name only) or gives the disclosure but fails to properly introduce themselves .
column5: Fair - The Agent introduces themselves, their company, and provides the call recording disclosure, meeting the minimum requirements .
column6: Good - The Agent provides a full introduction and disclosure in a professional and clear tone, and states the purpose of the call .
column7: Excellent - The Agent completes all requirements of 'Good' while also using a warm and courteous greeting (e.g., "Good morning"), effectively building rapport from the start of the call.

column2: Not Required - If the agent is never connected to a live representative, then the agent is unable to verify the account.
column3: Incomplete - The Agent fails to provide any of the necessary information to locate the client's account .
column4: Poor - The Agent provides only one of the required verification points (name, account #, or SSN), causing delays .
column5: Fair - The Agent provides some, but not all, of the required information, requiring the representative to prompt for the missing details .
column6: Good - The Agent clearly and accurately provides all required information (client name, account number, last four of SSN) allowing the representative to locate the account efficiently .
column7: Excellent - The Agent completes all requirements of 'Good' and proactively confirms the representative has located the correct account before proceeding, ensuring accuracy.

column2: Not Required - If the creditor does not ask for ATC/POA, or otherwise states that they already see authorization on file, then the agent does not need to resend ATC/POA to the creditor.
column3: Incomplete - If the ATC was not on file, the agent proceeds to continue or end the call without confirming any of the required processing details (method or timeline), resulting in a major compliance lapse and likely delay.
column4: Poor -  If the ATC was not on file, the agent successfully confirmed one of the required details (either the method for sending the document OR the processing timeline), but failed to confirm or clearly document the other. Compliance was partially met, but the next steps remain vague.
column5: Fair -  If the ATC was not on file, the agent clearly confirmed the method for sending the document AND the timeline for processing (whether it could be processed on the call or the specific delay). All compliance requirements for documenting the ATC status were met.
column6: Good - If the ATC was not on file, the agent clearly confirmed the method for sending the document and the timeline for processing (whether it could be processed on the call or the specific delay), in addition the agent seeks to get the ATC processed during the call to expedite processing.
column7: Excellent - The agent performed all steps required for a "Good" rating flawlessly. Additionally, the agent handled the situation with exceptional clarity and efficiency, proactively confirming the next steps back to the creditor (e.g., "So, I will fax the document immediately, and you confirm we should see processing complete within 24 hours?"). The agent ensured zero ambiguity and established a clear path forward for the client.

column2: Not Required - If the creditor is unable to locate the client or account, or states that the account has been sent to another creditor, then the agent is unable to verify information.
column3: Incomplete - The Agent fails to request account information, like balance, and does not present client hardship if asked
column4: Poor - The agent fails to either ask for account information, like the balance, or fails to present hardship information if asked, but does not fail to do both.
column5: Fair - The Agent confirms the account information, but is unprepared to provide a hardship reason if prompted, causing delays in the call.
column6: Good - The Agent confirms the current account balance, and provides the client's hardship reason if prompted .
column7: Excellent - The Agent completes all requirements of 'Good' and offers or presents the hardship in a way that is utilized as leverage for negotiations.

column2: Not Required - If an account/client is unable to be located, or the account is not yet eligible for settlement, then negotiations will not occur.
column3: Incomplete - The agent does not present a settlement offer if eligible, and does not attempt to hold firm or counter the creditor's initial offer.
column4: Poor - The agent makes an initial offer but does not attempt to negotiate if the creditor pushes back, or accepts the creditor's first offer without attempting to negotiate better terms.
column5: Fair - The agent makes an initial offer but fails to be firm in their offer, or makes only a weak attempt to counter a creditor's initial offer.
column6: Good - The agent makes an initial offer and is firm with the offer if countered, or if the creditor makes the initial offer the agent makes a decisive counter offer or negotiates to a better offer.
column7: Excellent - A definitive outcome is reached where the Agent's initial offer is approved, or if challenged, the Agent confidently holds firm to secure the best possible outcome for the client.

column2: Not Required - If an account/client is unable to be located, or the account is not yet eligible for settlement, then negotiations will not occur, and a counter offer will not be made, and no settlement outcome will be reached.
column3: Incomplete - No outcome is reached, and neither the agent nor the creditor make a counter offer to the first presented offer.
column4: Poor - If counter offered the Agent fails to acknowledge or accurately record its terms, and either no outcome is reached or the agent accepts the counter offer without pushback.
column5: Fair - If countered offered, the Agent acknowledges the counter offer but fails to confirm all specific details, and an outcome for the settlement is reached.
column6: Good - If counter offered the Agent clearly acknowledges the counter offer, repeats the specific terms back to the representative to ensure accuracy, and an outcome for the settlement is reached.
column7: Excellent - The Agent completes all requirements of 'Good' and also manages expectations by asking the representative for a clear timeframe for the SIF/Offer Letter to be sent/processed.

column2: Not Required - If no settlement discussion occurs, or an account is unable to reach agreed upon terms during the call, then the payment arrangement will not be required to be presented/reviewed.
column3: Incomplete - An offer is approved, but no payment schedule details are discussed or confirmed.
column4: Poor - A payment arrangement is mentioned, but the Agent fails to confirm the specific details like amounts, dates, or number of payments.
column5: Fair - The Agent confirms most, but not all, of the required payment schedule details, leaving some ambiguity.
column6: Good - Following an approved offer, the Agent clearly outlines all required components: the number of payments, their specific amounts, and the start date, and agent asks when the SIF/Settlement/Offer letter should be received.
column7: Excellent - The Agent completes all requirements of 'Good' and also confirms additional logistical details such as the payment method and frequency, ensuring perfect clarity for all parties.

column2: Not Required - If the call is disconnected before the agent has a chance to give their closing, or if the call never connects to a live representative, or on a multiple account call Closing is only required on the final account.
column3: Incomplete - The Agent ends the call abruptly with no closing statement .
column4: Poor - The Agent ends the call without thanking the representative or confirming the call's business is concluded .
column5: Fair - The Agent confirms the call's business is concluded or thanks the representative for their assistance but not both.
column6: Good - The Agent confirms the calls business is concluded, offers a sincere thank you for the representative's time, and ends the call professionally.
column7: Excellent - The Agent completes all requirements of 'Good' and adds a forward-looking or rapport-building statement (e.g., "If I have more, I'll call back"), leaving a lasting positive impression.
